children: U.S. stocks moved higher Friday as investors returned to equities after four consecutive losing sessions, while retreating crude prices eased some pressure on markets despite renewed concerns about inflation and Federal Reserve policy.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained about 1%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite climbed roughly 1.1% and 1%, respectively. The gains came as oil prices pulled back after a recent rally tied to escalating Middle East tensions.
West Texas Intermediate crude fell 3% to $99.44 a barrel, while Brent declined 2.74% to $104.68. Both benchmarks remained on track for weekly gains of about 8%.

August consumer prices rose 0.4% from the prior month and 3.4% from a year earlier. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, increased 0.3% monthly, with the annual rate at 2.4%. The data was broadly in line with forecasts, although core inflation exceeded expectations.

Treasury yields were mostly steady, with the two-year yield reaching its highest level since July 2024. Market pricing indicated an 85.6% probability of a quarter-point Federal Reserve rate increase the following week.

title: Nasdaq Snaps Four-Day Losing Streak as Oil Prices Retreat
